definition: Zero Trust Access (ZTA) is a security model that employs micro-segmentation, continuous monitoring, and ongoing validation of devices and users to enforce granular access controls, ensuring every access request is scrutinized regardless of its origin. VPNs encrypt data in transit to protect against interception but offer less granular control over user access and were designed for centralized network models, creating performance issues and security gaps in dispersed, cloud-centric environments. The key distinction is that ZTA reduces the potential attack surface through precise, continuously enforced controls, while VPNs may expose more of the network than necessary and struggle to adapt to modern hybrid and multi-cloud architectures.
